package store

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/pkg/errors"

	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/base"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/storage/s3"
	storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
)

type Attachment struct {
	// ID is the system generated unique identifier for the attachment.
	ID int32
	// UID is the user defined unique identifier for the attachment.
	UID string

	// Standard fields
	CreatorID int32
	CreatedTs int64
	UpdatedTs int64

	// Domain specific fields
	Filename    string
	Blob        []byte
	Type        string
	Size        int64
	StorageType storepb.AttachmentStorageType
	Reference   string
	Payload     *storepb.AttachmentPayload

	// The related memo ID.
	MemoID *int32

	// Composed field
	MemoUID *string

value.text:
q15.

| Table | Struct — path |
| --- | --- |
| `user` | `store.User` — `store/user.go` (line 29) |
| `attachment` | `store.Attachment` — `store/attachment.go` (line 16) |
| `reaction` | `store.Reaction` — `store/reaction.go` (line 7) |

These are plain Go structs rather than ORM models, so the table mapping comes from the hand-written SQL in the driver packages that scan into them: `store/db/sqlite/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go` (`FROM user` / `FROM "user"`), `store/db/sqlite/attachment.go` and `store/db/postgres/attachment.go` (`INSERT INTO attachment`), and `store/db/sqlite/reaction.go` and `store/db/postgres/reaction.go` (`FROM reaction`). The schema definitions themselves live under `store/migration`.

Note that the same names also exist as generated protobuf API types in `proto/gen/api/v1/user_service.pb.go`, `proto/gen/api/v1/attachment_service.pb.go`, and `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go` (`Reaction`), but those are wire/API messages, not table mappings.
